candidate.statement: A shared FIFO queue is accessed concurrently by multiple producers and consumers. Identify the critical section boundaries, explain the trade-offs of lock acquisition scope (coarse-grained outside loop vs fine-grained inside loop), and explain what failure occurs if an exception bypasses lock release.
hints: Critical section encompasses any access to shared pointers, size counters, or internal buffers.
short_diagnostics: Why must lock release be guaranteed via RAII or try/finally blocks?

evaluator.reference_solution: The critical section must enclose all mutations and reads of queue head/tail pointers and item count. Coarse locking outside loops reduces lock overhead but serializes entire batches, starving other threads; fine locking inside loops maximizes concurrency at the cost of higher lock acquisition overhead. Unhandled exceptions that bypass lock release cause permanent deadlock as other waiting threads block indefinitely.
evaluator.rubric: Accurately defines critical section bounds, lock granularity trade-offs, and deadlock risk from unreleased mutexes.
known_pitfalls: Enclosing non-shared I/O operations inside the critical section.
